subject: Air-gapped deployment — Exhibit F scope & limited audit window
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@staterahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Air-gapped deployment — Exhibit F scope & limited audit window

Daniel —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As we discussed, Statera’s procurement/legal has asked for clearer language around what Redwood will provide for an air-gapped (on‑prem) deployment and the expectations for any access or audit activity. To keep the MSA/Order Form narrow and operationally feasible, we propose: 

- Exhibit F to define a limited "Audit Window" (up to 72 hours per calendar year, scheduled with 7 business days' notice).
- Redwood to provide a signed environment snapshot hash and remote attestation artifacts (no handover of source code or build artifacts).
- Onsite observation limited to proof-of-access activities; if Statera requires deeper inspection, we propose a paid professional services engagement.

Attached: proposed-exhibitF-redline.pdf (high‑level redlines and alternate language). Can you confirm whether this approach would be acceptable to your team, or suggest non‑negotiable contract language you need?

If useful, I can schedule a 30‑minute redline session next week with your procurement + your outside counsel.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0119
[Attachment: proposed-exhibitF-redline.pdf (PDF, 128KB)]

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@staterahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@staterahealth.com>, Gibson Dunn <contracts@gibsondunn.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment — Exhibit F scope & limited audit window

Ben —

Appreciate the draft. High level: Statera needs a mechanism to verify operator access and that production code can be reproduced in our own environment if necessary. We are not asking for source code escrow, but procurement wants a firm path for (a) evidence of environment provenance and (b) a defined redress/remediation step if operator access fails.

Two quick asks from legal/procurement after reviewing your PDF: 
1) Clarify what "remote attestation artifacts" include (signing keys? binary hashes? runtime provenance?).
2) If Redwood relies on notarized hashes, we need a chain-of-trust description we can share with counsel.

I've attached our ops/security profile to show the level of detail they expect. If you can provide a short writeup and an updated Exhibit F, procurement is happy to review.

-Daniel

Daniel Park
Head of Procurement, Statera Health
daniel.park@staterahealth.com
[Attachment: statera-ops-security-profile.pdf (PDF, 84KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@staterahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-06T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment — Exhibit F scope & limited audit window

Daniel —

Thanks — quick clarification below and an alternate path we think will address procurement without introducing escrow.

What we mean by "remote attestation artifacts":
- Signed build hashes (SHA‑256) produced by our build pipeline, timestamped and signed by Redwood's release signing key.
- Runtime manifest (container images, package checksums) and a short provenance statement describing the build inputs.
- Audit log extract for the operator account showing last successful authentication and role actions for the 30 days prior to a requested Audit Window.

Alternative (preferred) path: a rolling snapshot deposit. Redwood will publish a notarized digest (hash) of the deployed artifact to an immutable ledger (third‑party timestamping service) monthly. On a scheduled Audit Window we can provide the signed digest and a controlled remote verification session (read‑only), plus a short onsite witness period (max 8 hours) if you need physical confirmation.

If that addresses counsel's chain-of-trust question, Laura — can your team draft a concise Exhibit F paragraph (2–3 clauses) that we can propose back to Statera? I attached a sample text we use internally.

Ben
[Attachment: proposed-exhibitF-redline.pdf (updated)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment — Exhibit F scope & limited audit window

Ben / Jonas —

Draft paragraph below you can propose to Statera. This is intentionally narrow and focused on verification rather than transfer: 

"Exhibit F — Limited Verification and Audit Window: Redwood will provide notarized build digests and runtime manifests sufficient to verify artifact provenance. Customer may request a scheduled Audit Window (no more than 72 hours per calendar year) to remotely verify the deployed environment via read-only access and a controlled witness session; onsite inspection beyond read-only verification must be agreed in advance and will be scoped as professional services. Redwood shall not be required to escrow source code or internal build systems under this Exhibit. Any access provided will be subject to mutually agreed access procedures and confidentiality protections."

Two operational notes: 
- Add an SLA carveout line: acceptance testing for the Audit Window will not be used to extend SLAs or trigger credits.
- Add retention schedule reference: logs provided for verification will be limited to 90 days unless otherwise negotiated.

Attached: exhibitF-draft-msar-lines.txt with the clause formatted for insertion into the MSA. Let me know if you want a version that references a specific timestamping provider.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: exhibitF-draft-msar-lines.txt (TXT, 3KB)]

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@staterahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@staterahealth.com>, Gibson Dunn <contracts@gibsondunn.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T15:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment — Exhibit F scope & limited audit window

Ben / Laura —

This is helpful — thanks. Procurement and counsel reviewed the proposed Exhibit F language and are comfortable with the narrow verification approach and the 72‑hour annual window, subject to two items: 

1) We'd like a pilot acceptance path: 2‑week pilot where Redwood performs the monthly notarized digest publication and one 48‑hour remote verification session. If the pilot passes, Statera will sign the Order Form and proceed to production.

2) Please include a mutually agreed escalation path if operator access fails (contact list, response SLA, and remediation steps).

I've attached our updated Order Form (orderform-v2.docx) with the pilot and acceptance language inserted. If Redwood is good, please upload to DocuSign (link below) and send final redlines by EOD Friday.

DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/ordering/RDW-2027-337-orderform-v2

Talk soon —
Daniel

Daniel Park
Head of Procurement, Statera Health
